answer: In a poll on using a cipher to protect data about the zenith of ferrous production, rostered keys may delegate their vote. The server checks election-bound signatures and sequence numbers, rejecting invalid messages; a direct ballot overrides delegation, and the highest sequence wins among conflicting messages of the same type. Each key contributes one vote, cast directly or by its delegate. More delegated weight requires more authorizations, potentially costing persuasion effort. Shared keys enable abuse, and unlisted people are excluded.
